dedupe_keys.name: højvandsstatistikker 2024 extreme water level statistics for danish waters

description: Højvandsstatistikker 2024 are the statistics of extreme water levels in Danish waters prepared by the Danish Coastal Authority. The 2024 edition updates the 2017 statistics and covers the period from the last revision to 31 December 2023. It was revised in November 2024: data were corrected at some places, statistics for Nykøbing Mors were added (which changed the numbering of the following data sheets), the 200-year event was removed because the uncertainty of such a long extrapolation is too large for the length of the data series, the isostatic uplift for Bornholm was corrected to the values of the Swedish Lantmäteriet, and the remarks now flag where extrapolation is especially uncertain. The statistics are used mainly for coastal flood hazard, for recommending the lowest building levels and for specific coastal construction projects, and the page stresses that local conditions along each stretch of coast must be assessed. Access is free on the page; no licence is stated. Caveats: the 200-year event is no longer given, and results apply to the coastal stretch each station represents. Coverage is the Danish coast. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation analysis, such as design water levels for ports, coastal roads and flood defences; the related record is Kystdata.
